proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/fork-cut.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd

mutations.cell: the step forked at is NOT in the cut: the child re-runs it

mutations.name: the cut is computed in RESUME mode
mutations.expectRed: the real plan reaches a cut inside a settled scope, because it walks in migration mode
mutations.cell: the real plan reaches a cut inside a settled scope, because it walks in migration mode

mutations.name: the child is reseeded from its own run id
mutations.find: await createRunSpec(kv, endpoint, plan.child, { pins: plan.pins, createdAt: plan.at });

mutations.expectRed: it is pinned to the parent's seed, so the copied prefix decides what it decided

mutations.cell: and leaves NO record behind: the spec is written last

mutations.cell: with L5001, the divergence, not with a cut refusal

} else if (err instanceof UnwalkableScope) {
      /* mutated: the refusal is dropped */
mutations.expectRed: a fork past a settled conclave is refused with L5014, not waved through
mutations.cell: a fork past a settled conclave is refused with L5014, not waved through
mutations.note: Graduated from fork-unasserted.json on 2026-08-16. It SURVIVED there — nothing watched L5014 — and is predicted KILLED here now that a cell does.

mutations.name: L5018 rides along beside a refusal that already explains the stop
mutations.expectRed: and NOT with L5018, which would send the caller to repair a step key that is correct
mutations.cell: and NOT with L5018, which would send the caller to repair a step key that is correct

mutations.name: the L5018 gate is too broad and suppresses a genuinely unreached step
mutations.expectRed: with L5018, because a cut never reached is the whole journal
mutations.cell: with L5018, because a cut never reached is the whole journal
mutations.note: The twin of the mutation above. One proves the gate FIRES; this proves it does not fire for everything — a gate that suppressed L5018 outright would pass the first mutation and lose the refusal.

mutations.name: the enclosing scope is copied settled, so the child short-circuits past its own cut
mutations.expectRed: the CHILD's first live step is the step it was forked to re-run, not the one after the scope
mutations.cell: the CHILD's first live step is the step it was forked to re-run, not the one after the scope
mutations.note: Named on the CHILD-RUN cell on purpose, not on a plan-shape cell. Several plan-shape cells also redden, but they are the kind of assertion that let claim 1 survive 200 trials; the mutation is graded on the one that runs the child.

mutations.name: a cut inside a decided race is admitted instead of refused
mutations.expectRed: a cut inside a decided `race` is refused with L5020 rather than re-raced
mutations.cell: a cut inside a decided `race` is refused with L5020 rather than re-raced

mutations.name: the projection is too broad and drops scopes that do NOT enclose the cut
mutations.expectRed: and the scope it does not enclose STAYS in the prefix: the projection is enclosing-only
mutations.cell: so the CHILD replays that scope instead of re-entering it: it records no second `parallel:pair`
mutations.note: The narrowness twin. Projecting EVERY scope entry would satisfy the first mutation perfectly while destroying any fork whose cut sits after an unrelated combinator -- the child would re-enter and re-run scopes it had already settled. It SURVIVED its first grading and survived honestly: it was graded on `a fork at a recorded step is admissible`, a cell over a program with NO SCOPES, so the widening could not change its answer. Re-graded on a child seeded from a cut taken AFTER a settled `parallel`, and on what that child APPENDS -- the branch sleeps replay either way, so the first-live-step probe is inert here and only the second `parallel:pair#0` row tells the two apart.

mutations.name: L5020 is dropped from the ride-along gate
mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: L5018 no longer rides along, because the step IS one the program reaches
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: L5018 no longer rides along, because the step IS one the program reaches
mutations.note: The gate's narrowness is graded by mutation 12 (`the L5018 gate is too broad`), which is why no twin is added here: a gate that swallowed L5018 for every stop would satisfy this removal and be caught there.

mutations.name: the gate runs before the projection, so it cannot see L5020
mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: L5018 no longer rides along, because the step IS one the program reaches
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: L5018 no longer rides along, because the step IS one the program reaches
mutations.note: ORDERING, mutated as its own fact. The repair was not only adding a code to the gate -- it was moving the gate BELOW the projection that pushes L5020. An empty set stands in for the ordering bug the move fixed: a `some()` over a refusal list that has not been filled yet is a check that cannot fail, and it reads identically to a correct gate.

mutations.name: a refused plan hands its cut back anyway
mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: an INADMISSIBLE plan carries no cut
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: an INADMISSIBLE plan carries no cut

mutations.name: the cut is emptied for everyone, refused or not
mutations.expectRed: and an admissible plan over the same journal still carries its prefix
mutations.cell: and an admissible plan over the same journal still carries its prefix
mutations.note: The narrowness twin. `cut = []` unconditionally satisfies the removal above perfectly and makes every fork a fork of nothing -- admissible, empty-prefixed, and silent. Graded on the control cell in the same block rather than on a distant one, so the two mutations differ by exactly the condition under test.

mutations.name: the plan addresses the caller's raw list again
mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: the cut carries one row per step, folded by the journal rather than by a second rule
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: the cut carries one row per step, folded by the journal rather than by a second rule
mutations.note: The defect exactly as it shipped, and it is invisible to every other block in this file because they all build a KEYED view with `Journal.entries()`. Only the block that hands `planFork` an append log -- the shape a driver actually holds -- can see it.

mutations.name: the fold returns nothing, so every fork is a fork of no history
mutations.expectRed: the cut is what happened BEFORE it
mutations.cell: the cut is what happened BEFORE it
mutations.note: The narrowness twin. An empty fold satisfies the mutation above perfectly -- one row per step is trivially true of no rows -- and hands every child an empty prefix, which is admissible, silent, and wrong. Graded on block 1's cut, the plainest statement of what a prefix is, because this suite counts rather than throws and a broad mutation may redden more than the cell it names.

unkillable.name: an activation expecting a NEW run accepts one whose journal has records
unkillable.why: Unkillable FROM HERE, and recorded rather than dropped. This suite imports @cotal-ai/core, whose package exports resolve to `dist`, so a mutation of core's SOURCE cannot reach it without a rebuild — the harness reported SURVIVED, which was honest: the suite genuinely does not exercise the mutated file in this configuration. The cell that observes this fence is real and lives here; the KILL for the guard belongs to a core suite that imports core from `../src`. Recorded so that a later reader does not re-author this mutation and read SURVIVED as a missing test.

unkillable.name: the `reached` clause of the cut's gate
unkillable.why: Ungradable from any suite, because it is now REDUNDANT and that is deliberate. The gate reads `reached && refusals.length === 0`, and the second clause subsumes the first on every path this source has: unreached-and-unrecorded pushes L5017; unreached-and-recorded pushes L5018 unless L5001/L5014/L5020 already explains the stop. So `!reached` always arrives carrying a refusal, removing `reached &&` changes no observable answer, and a mutation on it can only ever report SURVIVED -- indistinguishable from a missing test. It is kept as defence in depth against a FUTURE path that returns unreached with an EMPTY refusal set, which would hand a plausible cut back silently. The premise that makes it redundant is itself asserted, by `an unreached plan always carries a refusal, which is what makes its empty cut overdetermined`: the day that cell fails, this mutation becomes gradable again and belongs back in the set.
unkillable.history: It was a graded mutation until this repair. It has now gone ERROR -- anchor line rewritten, nothing mutated -- TWICE in one day, once for the projection repair and once for this one, the second time after the rule about it was already written down. Re-anchoring it a third time would have hidden the real change, which is that the guard it grades stopped being observable.
